# DSPy Field Guide

> A concept-level field guide to the DSPy codebase, written by Doc Holiday
> (https://doc.holiday) by exploring the DSPy source directly. Each page explains why a
> subsystem exists, its central abstractions, and how it relates to its neighbors.
> Every doc page is also served as plain Markdown — append `/index.md` to any page URL.

## Pages

- [The Big Picture](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/the-big-picture/): the Signature→Module→Adapter→LM spine
- [Anatomy of a Call](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/anatomy-of-a-call/): end-to-end trace of one module call
- [The LM Layer](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/the-lm-layer/): how a model string becomes a provider request
- [Caching](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/caching/): the cache, its key, and its footguns
- [What Compile Does](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/what-compile-does/): what optimizers actually mutate
- [Inside MIPROv2](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/inside-miprov2/): the flagship optimizer's mechanism — bootstrapped demos, proposed instructions, and Optuna-guided search
- [The Proposer](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/the-proposer/): how DSPy writes instruction candidates
- [Streaming](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/streaming/): token streaming vs typed parsing
- [Production](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/production/): callbacks, usage tracking, parallelism
- [About This Site](https://doc.holiday/library/dspy/about-this-site/): scope, audience, provenance

## See also

- Official DSPy documentation: https://dspy.ai/
- DSPy source: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy
